description: The bar chart illustrates the % point difference in morphosyntactic probing performance between two multilingual BERT models — mBERT (light blue) and XLM-R (dark blue) — across four different hidden layer configurations: “hidden:[50], linear”, “hidden:[], linear”, “hidden:[100], ReLU”, and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU”. The vertical axis represents the percentage point difference, ranging from -0.2 to +0.2, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Each configuration has two adjacent bars, one for each model, with mBERT consistently shown in light blue and XLM-R in dark blue. For “hidden:[50], linear”, mBERT shows a negative difference of approximately -0.18, while XLM-R is slightly less negative at around -0.07. In “hidden:[], linear”, both models show positive differences, with mBERT at ~+0.07 and XLM-R at ~+0.20. For “hidden:[100], ReLU”, mBERT is at ~-0.11 and XLM-R is slightly positive at ~+0.03. Finally, in “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU”, mBERT is at ~-0.18 and XLM-R is at ~-0.12. The chart suggests that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT in these probing tasks, particularly in the “hidden:[], linear” configuration, where it achieves the highest positive difference. The bars are grouped by configuration along the horizontal axis, and no sorting is applied — the configurations appear in the order listed. A small gray square in the legend likely indicates a placeholder or unused category.
